supersededRates.why: CO₂ from energy over total energy supply, which leaves out the cement and industrial CO₂ the slider carries

inputs.label: People in 2100
inputs.help: The UN projects 10.2 billion, with a 95% range of about 9 to 11.4.

inputs.label: Income growth per person
inputs.help: The world averaged 1.91% a year from 1990 to 2024.

inputs.label: Energy needed per dollar
inputs.help: Energy per dollar improved 1.43% a year since 1990, the largest of the four factors over that period.

inputs.label: Carbon per unit of energy
inputs.help: The fuel mix improved 0.15% a year since 1990 and 0.40% over the past decade, on the same basis as the scenarios, cement and industrial CO₂ included.

inputs.label: Land use CO₂ in 2100
inputs.help: Forests and farming release about 3.8 Gt a year now. CMIP7 spans a sink of 8.8 Gt to a source of 1.9. Regrowth and restoration net into this figure; engineered removal has a slider of its own.

inputs.label: Methane in 2100
inputs.help: The world emits about 380 Mt a year now. CMIP7 spans 94 in VERY LOW to 533 in HIGH.

inputs.label: Improvement delivered by 2062
inputs.help: The rate sliders set the 2100 level of energy per dollar and CO₂ per unit of energy. This sets how that change spreads across the years between. Half by the midpoint gives a constant rate; above half puts more of the change in the first half of the century.

inputs.label: Engineered CO₂ removal in 2100
inputs.help: Bioenergy with capture, direct air capture and the rest: removal that stores carbon outside the land account. Forests and soils sit on the land use slider, so neither counts the same tonne. A product of four positive factors stays above zero at any rate, and this term takes a path below it. The ramp starts slowly and steepens, as in the scenarios.

rateProducts.note: energy x CO₂ rate products, and all three including income, counted exactly
